acceptance_criteria: An Xcode project builds an iOS app and an embedded widget extension
Demo fans support power, speed, mode, light level and countdown
App Intents expose parameterized fan controls to Shortcuts
Widgets offer configurable demo fan controls
Demo and live connectivity are explicitly separated
A beginner guide explains the files and SwiftUI data flow
The user-provided basic SDK is integrated without adding AI features
Private SDK settings can be entered in the app and saved in Keychain
The connection flow compiles against actual SDK headers and setup UI tests pass
Wi-Fi detection uses public Apple APIs in eligible builds; Personal Team builds clearly offer manual entry without location prompts
Pairing and home use native fan artwork with Reduce Motion aware connecting animation
Pairing has independent token/hotspot/activation deadlines and shows real SDK stages and error codes
Unsupported EZ is blocked; AP guide uses supplied remote image and distinguishes fast from slow blinking
Foreground return during pairing does not refresh the cloud home on a no-internet fan hotspot
Live controls use icon selectors instead of enum dropdowns and support SDK renaming
A connected-fan widget reads last-reported display snapshots and opens live controls; demo widget stays distinct
Fan detail opens full screen from Home and widget routes without a full-sheet glass surface
Home preserves direct fan actions and summarizes actual running fans and lights
Light choices fill their row evenly and fan controls have more vertical spacing with a taller power selector
Home offers opt-in approximate-location weather with denied/network failure feedback and visible attribution
Home shows actual fan/light counts and nonblocking header refresh animation respecting Reduce Motion
hardware_control: Requires the user to configure the app on their phone and activate one fan; compilation and setup UI checks are not proof of hardware compatibility
